methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: A liberal arts college in Southwest Virginia launching a WorkAI Lab signals distributed capacity-building outside traditional tech hubs, creating peer networks for AI fluency in historically underserved regions—exactly the infrastructure needed for broad, deep adoption.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads by a Norfolk native directly targets the 'technology gap' with grassroots skill-building, signaling distributed peer-to-peer knowledge transfer rather than platform dependency or concentration in established metros.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ data center infrastructure investment in Henrico adds 200 jobs but concentrates AI-enabling infrastructure in an existing metro hub, reinforcing Richmond's position while rural areas remain infrastructure-poor—deepening rather than bridging the capability geography.

signals.title: Richmond summer program helps visually impaired students explore careers in technology and cybersecurity - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: A specialized summer program teaching visually impaired students cybersecurity and tech careers demonstrates targeted capacity-building for traditionally excluded populations, signaling intentional distribution of deep technical skills beyond typical access pathways.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech adding an AI minor concentrates advanced curriculum development in an established research university, creating deep expertise but primarily benefiting students already in higher-ed pipelines rather than distributing AI fluency through community channels.
